primary_test.what: split 1 (fitted on the report half, steered on the selection half), layer 19, gold_probe against 500 premise_balanced_probe controls (labellings with both balances of the gold label), one-sided in the sign of the 20-control run (-1), per unit of s
primary_test.abs_rank_per_natural_sd_note: a size, not a test: for probe directions the real direction has about twice the natural SD of every control, and ranks first in 12 to 41% of runs with no effect (tenth audit, F5)

second_question_the_label_beyond_adjacen.what_it_can_show: a positive result: the label has an effect beyond the one linear adjacency direction (not beyond graph structure in general). A null result shows nothing: the comparison has little power at the observed size, and a fifth of the items sit in single-class cells.

how_to_read.beyond_all_controls: moderate evidence for a label-specific effect: under a label-free response this happens in about 3% of runs if that response is isotropic and in 1 to 12% under the anisotropy the 20-control run allows
how_to_read.between_the_threshold_and_0.05: evidence for neither account: about as likely with a real effect of the observed size as without
how_to_read.above_0.05: moderate evidence against an effect of the observed size

primary_test.note: The direction of this split is not an independent draw: the gold direction fitted on the two halves is nearly one vector. p <= 0.05 here means only that this direction's slope is reproducibly in the tail of its controls, which choosing the most extreme of 24 comparisons would produce by itself; the threshold for that choice is 0.05/24.
